discrepancies: RxPrep uses a less-than-two-inch rule for selected first/second-degree self-care; current module must preserve depth, location, host and ABA consultation distinctions instead of teaching diameter alone.

RxPrep broadly prohibits SSD with sulfa allergy/G6PD deficiency. Label formally prohibits SSD/ingredient hypersensitivity and specified neonatal/pregnancy settings, while other sulfonamide cross-sensitivity and G6PD hemolysis are warnings requiring clinical assessment. The blanket healing claim is not retained: a limited adult RCT did not show an SSD healing advantage over petrolatum; narrow population and attrition constrain inference.
ABA first-aid text avoids ointments during initial cooling; AAD supports petroleum after cooling a minor first-degree burn. Teach timing and scope explicitly.
McGovern uses FFP for selected major burns; ABA 2024 recommends this resuscitation use only within research. National recommendation and center-specific practice are distinguished.

Vanderbilt May 2026 discourages routine empiric hydroxocobalamin for smoke exposure and asks for intensivist discussion. FDA label requires prompt treatment at high suspicion. Teach clinical selection versus routine use; do not convert the local policy into a blanket prohibition or delay for a cyanide test.
numericalReview: Adult rule of nines:9+2*9+2*18+18+18+1=100. New initial-rate case independently checked: 2*60*25=3000 mL; 3000/2/8=187.5 mL/hour, explicitly starting at injury time. Enter TBSA as percent points (30, not 0.30).
